svg.title: The L0–L8 native workspace
svg.desc: Layer map of the 115-crate native Rust workspace grouped into nine layers L0 to L8, dependencies pointing downward only. From the bottom: L0 support; L1, L2, L5 protocol, contracts, platform; L3 domain logic; L4, L6, L7 runtime, diagnostics, relay transports; L8 Android and JNI adapters, the only .so roots, behind a dashed JNI boundary. Only the 13 L8 crates may touch jni, and 11 do today.
svg.text: event loop · metrics · telemetry · relay protocol impls
desync engine · SOCKS5 · TUN pump · DNS · routing policy
protocol / core · contracts / config · platform / privileged
wire formats · error types · OS-level APIs (TUN, VpnService stub)
dev-dependencies only · test fixtures · build helpers
The data plane — SOCKS5, TUN pump, desync, relay, DNS — stays in Rust. JNI is crossed only to start/stop, poll telemetry, push a network snapshot, and VpnService.protect().
Every JNI export runs inside catch_unwind (ffi_boundary). The android-jni profile sets panic = "unwind".
